TITLE: Compliance gap analysis for financial institutions

hero.title: Compliance is a mosaic. We show which pieces are missing.
hero.lede: The Compliance assistant for financial institutions works out which Lithuanian and EU acts apply to you, checks each of their duties against your policies and writes a report with an action plan.
hero.fact: More than 50 acts from their official sources: the EU Publications Office, e-TAR and the Bank of Lithuania.

proof.title: A missing piece, up close
proof.lede: Every gap is a specific place in your document. A finding joins the act's duty to the passage of your document that decides it, and marks that passage.
proof.specimen: A sample finding: the regulation's duty, a passage of the company's document and the assessment

applies.title: Works out which acts apply to you
applies.text: It reads each act's scope and decides from the company profile: the act applies, will apply later, or its application still has to be confirmed. Every decision comes with its reasons.

compares.title: Checks every duty against your documents
compares.text: It reads every uploaded document in full and gives each duty one of five statuses. A finding carries a quote you can open in the document.

plans.title: Draws up the action plan
plans.text: Every open gap is closed by one action: who owns it, how much work it is and by when. Overlapping actions are merged into one.

report.title: A report you can check
report.lede: Every finding shows the duty, the assessment and the evidence. Click a quote and the document opens at that place. You can replace a finding with your own assessment, then approve the finished report and export it: a PDF for the board, Excel for the work.
report.link: The whole way from a conversation to a report
report.specimen: A sample report: the findings counted by status and the gravest gaps

chat.title: Ask about the law — the answer names the article
chat.lede: The assistant searches the official texts of the acts and puts the article beside its answer, with a link to the official text. What it has not read in the corpus it marks “(to verify)” — so you can tell checked text from the model's own knowledge.

points.language: It answers in the language you ask in.
points.documents: It reads the documents dropped into the conversation and checks their references to the law.
points.reports: It knows your company's reports: ask which gaps are critical.

chat.specimen: A sample conversation: a question about DORA and an answer citing the article

sources.title: The texts come from their official sources
sources.lede: The acts are taken from their official sources, split down to article, paragraph and point, and refreshed every week. Every reference leads to the official text.

cellar.name: EU Publications Office
cellar.text: EU regulations and directives: the newest consolidated version in force, in Lithuanian.

etar.name: e-TAR
etar.text: Lithuanian laws and secondary legislation: the edition valid today.

lb.name: Bank of Lithuania
lb.text: The compliance-function guidelines and the licensing procedure per institution type.

limits.title: What the assistant does not do

lawyer.title: It does not replace a lawyer
lawyer.text: It is an artificial intelligence system and its findings are an aid. A person can review and change every finding, and a person approves the report.

practice.title: It does not assess practice
practice.text: The analysis assesses what your documents set out. Whether a procedure is followed in practice is yours to check — the report says what to look at.

guess.title: It does not guess
guess.text: What the material provided cannot show is marked “not evidenced”. Acts whose application depends on unknown facts are not assessed until the questions are answered.
